score_notes.novelty: The 'sort-shuffle is biased' observation is well-known in JS circles (Rob Weir 2010, countless Stack Overflow answers), but the live side-by-side tally that turns the bias into a per-engine portrait is a fresh mechanism the catalogue lacks — only the browser can do it, and the engine-as-author twist is genuinely new.
score_notes.nuance: Concept and execution collapse cleanly: the spec's 'implementation-defined' wording is literally enacted by the canvas, and the surface gag (two squares, one grey, one patterned) carries the literate reading (the engine is the artist) without wall text — restraint is exemplary, nothing on the page explains the joke.
score_notes.narrative: Names Arp, Kenneth Martin, y-a-v-a's own A Chance of Order and Arranged According to the Laws of Chance, and the EU ballot; sits legibly on the chance↔order axis and answers the prior works by staging the bug as the new readymade — a real move in the twenty-year argument, not just a name-drop.
score_notes.craft: Two 12×12 canvases, a counter, a label — the smallest build that completes the thought; the code is clean, no decoration, no fallback, no apology, and the implementation-defined mechanism is the idea rather than scaffolding around it.
score_notes.wit: The dry joke lands twice: honest chance fades to grey (chance paints nothing), the bug paints a portrait of the sorter (the engine is the artist) — humour IS the mechanism, and the 'Edition: one per engine' line is a perfect deadpan closer.

rationale: A strong candidate that earns its place in the catalogue. The mechanism — tallying Fisher–Yates against the canonical sort-shuffle into live deviation canvases — is genuinely web-native and only the browser can do it, and the 'implementation-defined' framing turns a well-known JS gotcha into a precise art-historical argument about authorship, chance, and the engine as artist. Concept and execution are the same object (P1), the chance↔order axis is staged directly (P5), the build is minimal (P3), and the dry wit carries the idea without explanation (P9). It answers prior works (Arp, Kenneth Martin, y-a-v-a's own chance pieces) rather than repeating them.
reservations: The sort-shuffle bias is a familiar trope in JS pedagogy, so the novelty credit is modest rather than maximal; a casual viewer who doesn't know the ECMA-262 wording may need a beat to grasp why the right square is the point. None of these are gate failures.
revision_suggestion: Optional: a one-line engine readout (V8/SpiderMonkey/JavaScriptCore) under the right canvas would make the 'edition: one per engine' claim self-attesting and tighten the surface gag for viewers who don't know the spec.
